data.narrative:
Harbinger is a Series C transportation company that has raised $358M to date. The comparable universe comprises eight private frontier-transportation firms, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia; no public transportation peers were identified with sufficient comparability. The absence of listed public comps and the nascent stage of the peer set constrained multi-method triangulation.

Stage-progression analysis was the applicable valuation method. Using the $358M total raised as a proxy baseline, a conservative $100M entry point was selected to avoid anchoring to outlier funding rounds. Applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression to the next institutional stage yields an implied valuation of $170M. This method is most reliable when capital efficiency and market maturation are consistent with peer cohorts, though the frontier-transportation sector shows high variance in both dimensions.

The triangulated valuation range is $144M to $195M, centered on $170M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single applicable method rather than confirmation across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peer data (zero comps met narrow filters), making stage-progression assumptions the primary valuation lever. Unit economics, path to profitability, and competitive positioning relative to the five named peers would materially affect placement within or beyond the stated range.
